project_tracker_diagnostic: Annual; more robust than C. basalis; leaves opposite and usually bipinnately divided into threadlike segments; rays yellow with broad dark reddish-brown basal zones.

project_inclusion.learning_reason: Common and useful Central Texas field-learning taxon.

morphology_keys.habit: Erect branching herb, often somewhat taller/coarser than C. basalis.
morphology_keys.leaves: Opposite below, dissected into many narrow threadlike segments.
morphology_keys.heads: Showy yellow rays with broad maroon to reddish-brown bases; disks dark.
morphology_keys.phyllaries: Outer bracts often spreading beneath a broader inner involucre.
best_field_traits: Annual, usually branched with opposite lower leaves divided into very narrow linear/threadlike segments.
Yellow rays frequently have dark reddish-brown basal patches, but patch extent varies and cannot alone distinguish the species.
Inspect mature head underside: outer involucral bracts and inner bracts, plus flat cypselae, to distinguish from similar annual Coreopsis.
Compare Coreopsis basalis: often broader leaf segments and differing head/fruit characters; use paired measured leaves and phyllary/fruit photos rather than petal coloration alone.

photo_strategy.selection_logic: Prefer curated taxon photos plus multiple views from one Central Texas/Texas observation.
photo_strategy.remaining_need: NEEDS_DIAGNOSTIC_PHOTO: same-scale C. tinctoria versus C. basalis leaf segments, involucre underside and mature cypselae; annotation_pending until visible anatomy confirmed.
